question: What is the chemical symbol for gold?
fact: Au comes from the Latin word "aurum".

question: Which planet is closest to the Sun?
fact: A year on Mercury lasts just 88 Earth days.

question: Which gas do plants absorb for photosynthesis?
fact: Plants use sunlight to turn CO2 and water into sugar.

question: What is the largest organ of the human body?
fact: An adult's skin covers about two square metres.

question: What force pulls objects towards the Earth?
fact: Gravity keeps the Moon in orbit too.

question: Which planet is known as the Red Planet?
fact: Iron oxide, or rust, gives Mars its colour.

question: Which organelle is known as the powerhouse of the cell?
fact: Mitochondria produce most of a cell's ATP.

question: What is the hardest natural substance?
fact: Diamond scores 10 on the Mohs scale.

question: Which blood cells carry oxygen around the body?
fact: Haemoglobin in them binds the oxygen.

question: Which planet has a famous Great Red Spot?
fact: The storm has raged for at least 150 years.

question: Which metal is liquid at room temperature?
fact: Mercury melts at about minus 39 degrees Celsius.

question: What is the chemical formula of table salt?
fact: It is sodium chloride.

question: In which part of a human cell is most DNA found?
fact: Mitochondria carry a little DNA of their own.

question: Which galaxy contains our Solar System?
fact: Our galaxy holds hundreds of billions of stars.

question: Who developed the theory of general relativity?
fact: He published it in 1915.

question: Which mammal lays eggs?
fact: Platypuses and echidnas are called monotremes.

question: What is the SI unit of force?
fact: One newton accelerates 1 kg by 1 m/s squared.

question: What is the most abundant gas in Earth's atmosphere?
fact: Nitrogen makes up about 78 percent of air.

question: Which vitamin does skin produce in sunlight?
fact: It helps the body absorb calcium.

question: Roughly how fast does light travel in a vacuum?
fact: Light takes about 8 minutes to travel from the Sun to Earth.

question: What is the pH of pure water at room temperature?
fact: Values below 7 are acidic and above 7 are basic.

question: The Ring of Fire surrounds which ocean?
fact: About 90 percent of earthquakes occur along it.

question: Which organ produces insulin?
fact: Insulin controls blood sugar levels.

question: Which type of rock forms from cooled magma or lava?
fact: Granite and basalt are igneous rocks.

question: What is the SI unit of electrical resistance?
fact: It is named after Georg Ohm.

question: What is the atomic number of carbon?
fact: Carbon has six protons.

question: Who discovered penicillin in 1928?
fact: Fleming noticed mould killing bacteria on a dish.

question: What is the most abundant element in the universe?
fact: Hydrogen makes up roughly 75 percent of ordinary matter.

question: What is the SI unit of frequency?
fact: One hertz is one cycle per second.

question: Which organelle carries out photosynthesis?
fact: Chlorophyll in chloroplasts makes leaves green.

question: What is the name of the supercontinent that existed about 300 million years ago?
fact: Pangaea began splitting apart around 200 million years ago.

question: Which vitamin deficiency causes scurvy?
fact: Sailors once carried citrus fruit to prevent it.

question: Which book by Charles Darwin was published in 1859?
fact: Alfred Russel Wallace independently reached similar ideas.

question: The Sun is classified as which type of star?
fact: It is a G-type main-sequence star.

question: Which scale ranks the hardness of minerals?
fact: Talc is 1 and diamond is 10.

question: Which metal has the highest melting point?
fact: Tungsten melts at about 3,400 degrees Celsius.

question: Which part of the brain coordinates balance and movement?
fact: Cerebellum means "little brain" in Latin.

question: Which blood type is the universal donor for red blood cells?
fact: It lacks A, B and Rh antigens.

question: Which particle carries the electromagnetic force?
fact: Photons are quanta of light.

question: What is the smallest bone in the human body?
fact: The stapes is in the middle ear and is about 3 mm long.

question: What is the scientific study of fungi called?
fact: Yeasts, moulds and mushrooms are fungi.

question: Where two tectonic plates move apart, the boundary is called what?
fact: Mid-ocean ridges are divergent boundaries.

question: Lightning never strikes the same place twice.
fact: Tall structures such as the Empire State Building are hit many times a year.

question: Sound travels faster in water than in air.
fact: It moves about four times faster in water.

question: Diamond and graphite are both made of pure carbon.
fact: Only the arrangement of their atoms differs.

question: Humans use only 10 percent of their brains.
fact: Brain imaging shows activity throughout the whole brain.

question: Venus is the hottest planet in the Solar System.
fact: Its thick CO2 atmosphere traps heat at about 465 degrees Celsius.

question: A proton is much heavier than an electron.
fact: A proton has about 1,836 times the mass of an electron.

question: Antibiotics are effective against viral infections like the flu.
fact: Antibiotics kill bacteria, not viruses.

question: Spiders are insects.
fact: Spiders are arachnids with eight legs; insects have six.

question: Water expands when it freezes.
fact: That is why ice floats and pipes can burst.

question: At sea level, at what temperature in Celsius does water boil?
fact: Boiling point drops at higher altitudes.

question: How many bones does an adult human have?
fact: Babies are born with roughly 270 to 300 bones.

question: How many elements are on the periodic table?
fact: Oganesson, element 118, was named in 2016.

question: What is the speed of light in a vacuum, in km per second?
fact: It is exactly 299,792,458 metres per second.

question: How far is the Moon from Earth, on average, in kilometres?
fact: The Moon drifts about 3.8 cm farther each year.

question: How old is Earth, in billions of years?
fact: Radiometric dating of meteorites gives this age.

question: What is normal human body temperature in degrees Celsius?
fact: Normal readings vary from about 36.1 to 37.2.

question: How far is the Sun from Earth, in millions of kilometres?
fact: Light takes about 8 minutes to cover it.

question: How many teeth does a typical adult human have, including wisdom teeth?
fact: Many adults have fewer wisdom teeth.

question: Who formulated the three laws of planetary motion in the early 1600s?
fact: Kepler showed planets move in ellipses, not circles.

question: What is the most abundant protein in the human body?
fact: It makes up about a quarter of body protein.

question: Who discovered the electron in 1897?
fact: He won the 1906 Nobel Prize in Physics.

question: Which gas makes up most of Mars's thin atmosphere?
fact: Over 95 percent of the Martian atmosphere is CO2.

question: What is the SI unit of magnetic flux density?
fact: It is named after Nikola Tesla.

question: In which layer of the atmosphere is the ozone layer found?
fact: It absorbs most of the Sun's harmful ultraviolet rays.

question: What is the largest moon of Saturn?
fact: Titan has a thick atmosphere and lakes of liquid methane.

question: What is the SI base unit for the amount of a substance?
fact: One mole contains about 6.02 x 10^23 particles.

question: Which element has the chemical symbol Fe?
fact: Fe comes from the Latin "ferrum".

question: Which organ filters blood to make urine?
fact: Each kidney holds about a million tiny filters.

question: What do we call animals that eat both plants and meat?
fact: Humans, bears and pigs are omnivores.

question: Which planet is famous for its bright, wide rings?
fact: Its rings are made mostly of chunks of ice.

question: Which part of a plant takes in water from the soil?
fact: Roots also hold the plant firmly in place.

question: Which gas do humans breathe out?
fact: We breathe out water vapour too, which you can see on a cold day.

question: Which state of matter has its own fixed shape?
fact: Liquids take the shape of their container, and gases fill it.

question: How many legs does an insect have?
fact: Spiders have eight, so they are not insects.

question: What is the centre of an atom called?
fact: It holds protons and neutrons.

question: Which of these is a renewable source of energy?
fact: Wind turbines turn moving air into electricity.

question: Which scientist is famous for the laws of motion and universal gravitation?
fact: He also helped invent calculus.

question: A dolphin is what type of animal?
fact: Dolphins breathe air through a blowhole on top of the head.

question: Which element has the atomic number 1?
fact: It is the lightest element.

question: Which planet spins tilted almost on its side?
fact: Its axis is tilted by about 98 degrees.

question: What is the name of the cell division that makes two identical copies of a cell?
fact: Your skin cells divide this way to repair cuts.

question: What is the SI unit of electric current?
fact: It is named after the French physicist André-Marie Ampère.

question: Which part of the eye controls how much light gets in?
fact: The iris is the coloured ring around the pupil.

question: Which layer of the Earth lies between the crust and the core?
fact: It makes up most of the planet's volume.

question: Which star is the closest to our Sun?
fact: Its light takes over four years to reach us.

question: Which animal was the first mammal cloned from an adult cell?
fact: Dolly was born in Scotland in 1996.

question: Who developed the first successful polio vaccine in the 1950s?
fact: Salk famously chose not to patent it.

question: Who discovered radioactivity in 1896?
fact: He noticed uranium salts fogging photographic plates.

question: Plants lose water vapour through tiny pores on their leaves. What are these pores called?
fact: Each pore is flanked by two guard cells that open and close it.

question: Which cell organelle contains enzymes that break down waste?
fact: Lysosomes work like the cell's recycling bins.

question: Which gas gives rotten eggs their smell?
fact: Even tiny amounts are easy for our noses to detect.

question: What causes the seasons on Earth?
fact: The tilt means each hemisphere leans towards the Sun at different times of year.

question: The Moon makes its own light.
fact: It shines by reflecting sunlight.

question: Sound can travel through the vacuum of space.
fact: Sound needs a medium such as air or water to travel through.

question: Lightning can be hotter than the surface of the Sun.
fact: A bolt can heat the air around it to about 30,000 degrees Celsius.

question: Adults have fewer bones than newborn babies.
fact: Many of a baby's bones fuse together as they grow.

question: Different parts of the tongue detect only one taste each.
fact: The "tongue map" is a myth, as all tastes can be sensed across the tongue.

question: A day on Venus is longer than its year.
fact: Venus spins so slowly that one rotation takes longer than one trip round the Sun.

question: Bananas are slightly radioactive.
fact: They contain potassium, a tiny part of which is radioactive, and it is harmless.

question: How many planets are in our Solar System?
fact: Pluto was reclassified as a dwarf planet in 2006.

question: How many chambers does a human heart have?
fact: Two upper atria and two lower ventricles.

question: How many chromosomes are in a typical human cell?
fact: They come in 23 pairs, one from each parent.

question: About how many minutes does sunlight take to reach Earth?
fact: Sunlight travels roughly 150 million kilometres to get here.

question: About what percentage of Earth's air is oxygen?
fact: Most of the rest is nitrogen.

question: At what temperature in Celsius is absolute zero?
fact: It is the coldest temperature possible, where particles have almost no motion.

question: What is the main gas in natural gas?
fact: Methane is a powerful greenhouse gas when it leaks.

question: Which part of a cell builds proteins?
fact: Ribosomes read instructions copied from DNA.

question: Which planet has the shortest day?
fact: It spins once in under 10 hours.

question: What gas makes up most of the Sun?
fact: About three quarters of the Sun's mass is hydrogen.

question: What is the most common element in Earth's crust?
fact: It is locked up in rocks and minerals.

question: Which part of the brain mainly controls balance and coordination?
fact: Its name means "little brain".

question: What is the chemical symbol for potassium?
fact: K comes from its Latin name, kalium.

question: What is the edge around a black hole, beyond which nothing escapes, called?
fact: Not even light can come back out.

question: Which vitamin helps blood to clot?
fact: The K comes from "Koagulation", German for clotting.

question: What do we call animals that are most active at dawn and dusk?
fact: Cats and rabbits are crepuscular.

question: Which animal has the largest eyes of any living creature?
fact: Each eye is about the size of a football.

question: What are the tiny air sacs in the lungs called?
fact: Spread flat, they would cover around 70 square metres.

question: Which element is named after the Greek word for the Sun?
fact: It was found in sunlight before it was found on Earth.

question: About how fast does sound travel in air at 20 °C, in metres per second?
fact: That is roughly one kilometre every three seconds.

question: Which is the longest bone in the human body?
fact: The femur is the thigh bone.
